name: Lambchop
label: Merge
lede: A Nashville band that got its name from a lawyer's letter, its fans from Europe, and its songs from a man who laid hardwood floors for a living long after the records got good.

eras.title: Posterchild in the bedroom
eras.text: Three old high school classmates in Nashville made tapes in a bedroom and played wherever they could, especially the record shop run by Kurt Wagner's wife. The trio kept growing into a loose, oversized ensemble.

years.h: Kurt Wagner starts Posterchild with two high school friends
years.p: In Nashville, Kurt Wagner, bassist [[Marc Trovillion|4647a834-8c3e-4cbd-81cf-31ba1bb61353]] and guitarist Jim Watkins form a trio called Posterchild. They record in Trovillion's bedroom and self-release cassettes.
years.xp: Wagner, born in Nashville to Northern parents, had been to art school in Memphis and was working as a carpenter, laying wood floors. He kept that job long after the band started getting reviews.

years.h: Posterchild become regulars at Lucy's Record Shop
years.p: The growing band plays regularly at Lucy's Record Shop, the Nashville shop founded by Kurt Wagner's wife, Mary Mancini. By now it's seven people, including Jonathan Marx and drummer Steve Goodhue.

years.h: A split single with Crop Circle Hoax gets a lawyer's attention
years.p: Posterchild's split 7-inch with Crop Circle Hoax, An Open Fresca + A Moist Towelette, catches the ear of entertainment lawyer George Regis.

eras.title: Not REN, not Pinnacles of Cream
eras.text: A legal letter forced a new name, and Merge gave the renamed band a home. Pedal steel, sax and organ came in, and by Thriller Lambchop were chasing Muscle Shoals soul as much as Nashville country.

years.big: Not REN. Not Pinnacles of Cream. Lambchop.
years.h: Poster Children's lawyer sends a cease-and-desist
years.p: The Illinois band [[Poster Children|050f867a-ed04-4a38-9f6e-b9bf84ca664b]] objects to the name Posterchild. Kurt Wagner's band rejects REN and Pinnacles of Cream before settling on Lambchop.
years.xp: The renamed lineup added singer and saxophonist [[Deanna Varagona|d8e78a9c-0001-49aa-bbd1-c6a9031b9268]], pedal steel player [[Paul Niehaus|f84893b8-2c33-4218-adc4-4169954610d8]] and organist John Delworth.

years.h: Lambchop sign to Merge and release the single Nine
years.p: Merge, the Chapel Hill label run by [[Superchunk|61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384]]'s [[Mac McCaughan|8841967d-3914-4ab9-aca6-94781aa35288]] and [[Laura Ballance|1d11820c-e2a0-4ad7-8415-3d93c317c8cf]], puts out Lambchop's first single, Nine.

years.h: I Hope You're Sitting Down, a.k.a. Jack's Tulips
years.p: Lambchop's debut album on Merge, credited with two titles, one on each side of the sleeve.

years.h: How I Quit Smoking goes for the old Nashville sound
years.p: Strings and lush arrangements in the style of 1960s Nashville-sound records. Released on Merge, and in Europe on City Slang.

years.h: Drummer Paul Burch debuts on the Hank EP
years.p: Lambchop's Hank EP marks the first appearance of drummer [[Paul Burch|e55af1dd-fc5e-4651-8508-42686e983a02]].

years.h: Thriller: Muscle Shoals soul and three East River Pipe songs
years.p: AllMusic calls it sprawling and difficult. Kurt Wagner covers three songs by [[East River Pipe|0e56780b-b99c-4078-a098-bba329db985d]]'s F.M. Cornog and leans into Southern soul.

eras.title: Soul falsetto, European concert halls
eras.text: Kurt Wagner found a falsetto and Curtis Mayfield, backed his friend Vic Chesnutt, and made Nixon. Largely ignored at home, Lambchop were suddenly playing Europe's big rooms.

years.h: What Another Man Spills covers Curtis Mayfield
years.p: Soul covers of Curtis Mayfield and Frederick Knight songs, with Kurt Wagner's baritone jumping to a falsetto AllMusic compares to [[Prince|070d193a-845c-479f-980e-bef15710653e]].

years.cap: Vic Chesnutt, The Salesman and Bernadette (1998).
years.h: Lambchop back [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]] on The Salesman and Bernadette
years.p: The whole Lambchop ensemble becomes the Athens, Georgia songwriter Vic Chesnutt's backing band for his 1998 album.

years.h: Kurt Wagner and Josh Rouse make Chester
years.p: Kurt Wagner teams up with Nashville singer-songwriter [[Josh Rouse|023d64c9-93db-4a20-8c5c-2efa1a53481a]] on the collaborative album Chester.

years.h: Nixon, with a reading list in the liner notes
years.p: A soul-steeped record about American history, packaged with a bibliography. It's Lambchop's breakthrough, mostly in Europe.

years.h: A Nashville cult band headlines London's Royal Festival Hall
years.p: Barely known in the US, Lambchop play London's Royal Festival Hall. Limited European tour EPs follow, Queens Royal Trimma in 2000 and Treasure Chest of the Enemy in 2001.

years.h: Tools in the Dryer gathers Lambchop's odds and ends
years.p: Singles, compilation tracks and remixes in one place.

years.h: Is a Woman strips Lambchop to a whisper
years.p: After Nixon's horns and strings, a deliberately sparse, quiet album built around Kurt Wagner's voice and piano.

eras.title: Two albums on one day
eras.text: Lambchop went maximal again, releasing two records at once, then kept shifting shape with electronic collaborators and a stable of Nashville players like William Tyler and Tony Crow. The era closed with the death of Vic Chesnutt.

years.h: Aw Cmon and No You Cmon, released together
years.p: Two string-heavy albums, issued as a pair in February 2004.

years.h: CoLAB EP with electronic duo Hands Off Cuba
years.p: Lambchop cut an experimental EP with the Nashville electronic duo Hands Off Cuba, an early sign of where Kurt Wagner was headed.

years.h: The Woodwind Years, with a Gettysburg Address
years.p: The Decline of Country & Western Civilization, Pt. 2: The Woodwind Years mixes unreleased tracks with a new piece, Gettysburg Address.

years.h: Damaged, with William Tyler and Tony Crow
years.p: Fourteen songs, guitarist William Tyler and pianist Tony Crow in the core. Mojo calls it an album of colossal strength and maturity.

years.h: OH (Ohio)
years.p: Lambchop's tenth album, graceful and unhurried, per AllMusic.

years.h: [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]], Lambchop's friend and collaborator, dies
years.p: Vic Chesnutt, whose 1998 album Lambchop backed, dies on Christmas Day after an overdose of muscle relaxants. Kurt Wagner dedicates the next Lambchop album to him.

eras.title: For Vic, then for the machines
eras.text: Mr. M was a long goodbye to Vic Chesnutt. Then Lambchop lost a founder, and Kurt Wagner went off to make electronic music under another name, bringing it back into the band.

years.h: Mr. M: every song dedicated to Vic Chesnutt
years.p: Eleven string-laden songs about love and loss, the whole album dedicated to Vic Chesnutt's memory.

years.h: Founding bassist Marc Trovillion dies at 56
years.p: Marc Trovillion, who started Posterchild with Kurt Wagner in 1986 and recorded its first tapes in his bedroom, dies of a heart attack at 56.

years.h: Mary Mancini becomes Tennessee Democratic Party chair
years.p: Kurt Wagner's wife Mary Mancini, founder of Lucy's Record Shop, is elected chair of the Tennessee Democratic Party. She jokes that marrying a musician early helps with fundraising.

years.h: Kurt Wagner goes electronic as HeCTA
years.p: Kurt Wagner launches the electronic project HeCTA on Merge. Its sound feeds straight into the next Lambchop record.

years.h: FLOTUS: For Love Often Turns Us Still
years.p: Lambchop's electronic turn, Kurt Wagner's voice processed and floating over beats and orchestral arrangements.
years.xp: In 2017 Lambchop released The Hustle Unlimited, an orchestral rework of a FLOTUS track.

eras.title: Pen pals in lockdown
eras.text: Auto-Tune, a covers album, a pandemic and a paint factory in Minneapolis. Kurt Wagner rebuilt Lambchop around new collaborators, then found his next idea on late-night radio.

years.h: This (Is What I Wanted to Tell You) goes full Auto-Tune
years.p: Electronic textures and Auto-Tuned vocals from Kurt Wagner, another sharp turn for a band once filed under alt-country.

years.h: Trip, an album of cover songs
years.p: Lambchop release Trip, made up of covers, on Merge and City Slang.

years.h: Caring for his father, Kurt Wagner swaps music with Andrew Broder
years.p: While his father battles COVID, a stroke and hip surgery, Kurt Wagner trades files with Minneapolis musician Andrew Broder, turning Broder's piano improvisations into songs.

years.h: Showtunes, made remotely with James McNew
years.p: Kurt Wagner builds the album at a distance with [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]]'s [[James McNew|4182b4da-dc89-4331-bca0-952369bb63fb]], [[Ryan Olson|19bf8c5e-560c-4d85-98fb-51eb5fdc6c5d]] of Gayngs, DJ Twit One and producer Jeremy Ferguson.

years.h: The Bible, recorded in an old Minneapolis paint factory
years.p: Summer 2021 sessions in a former paint factory, produced by Andrew Broder and Ryan Olson with a crowd of local players, pull funk, R&B and jazz into Kurt Wagner's songs.

years.h: Punching the Clown and the lined-out gospel style
years.p: Driving at night, Kurt Wagner hears banjo-backed group singing on the radio and discovers lined-out hymn singing, call and response between a leader and a congregation. Punching the Clown sets new songs to a small choir.
